title: BRICKSTORM Backdoor Investigation
description: Investigate and mitigate the BRICKSTORM backdoor malware on the target system. This malware uses advanced techniques for evasion, including SOCKS proxying, multi-layered web service communication, and varied command execution.
outcomes: Understand the behavior of the BRICKSTORM backdoor malware.
Identify and investigate suspicious services and files.
Mitigate the threat by containing and removing the malware.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
The BRICKSTORM backdoor is a sophisticated malware family known for its advanced evasion techniques, including SOCKS proxying, multi-layered web service communication, and varied command execution. This malware has been detected on the target system, and your task is to investigate its behavior, identify its persistence mechanisms, and mitigate the threat. The investigation will involve analyzing systemd services, identifying suspicious files, and removing the malware to secure the system.

The BRICKSTORM backdoor is designed to maintain persistence on compromised systems, communicate with command and control (C2) servers, and execute malicious commands. It employs various techniques to evade detection, including the use of SOCKS proxying to hide its network traffic and multi-layered web service communication to obfuscate its C2 interactions.

levels.title: Identify the suspicious service related to the BRICKSTORM backdoor
levels.content:
The BRICKSTORM backdoor uses a persistence mechanism through a systemd service. Investigate the systemd services on the target system to identify the suspicious service. The flag you are looking for is the name of the service.

The BRICKSTORM backdoor communicates with its command and control (C2) server using multi-layered web service communication. The suspicious service is likely involved in maintaining this communication.

Steps:
1. SSH into the target system using the provided credentials.
2. List all systemd services and look for any suspicious services.
3. Identify the service related to the BRICKSTORM backdoor.
levels.solution:
The suspicious service related to the BRICKSTORM backdoor is backdoor-persistence.service.

Steps:
1. SSH into the target system using the provided credentials.
2. List all systemd services using the command: `systemctl list-units --type=service`.
3. Look for the service named backdoor-persistence.service.

hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system services.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all systemd services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The suspicious service is named backdoor-persistence.service.

levels.title: Investigate the suspicious file used by the BRICKSTORM backdoor
levels.content:
The BRICKSTORM backdoor uses a backdoor binary for its operations. Investigate the file system to identify the suspicious file. The flag you are looking for is the path to the binary.

The suspicious file is likely involved in executing commands from the C2 server and maintaining the backdoor's functionality. It may also be involved in SOCKS proxying to evade detection.

Steps:
1. SSH into the target system using the provided credentials.
2. Search the file system for suspicious files, especially in the `/usr/java/jre-vmware/bin` directory.
3. Identify the backdoor binary used by the BRICKSTORM malware.
levels.solution:
The suspicious file used by the BRICKSTORM backdoor is /usr/java/jre-vmware/bin/updatemgr.

Steps:
1. SSH into the target system using the provided credentials.
2. Search the file system for suspicious files using the command: `find / -name updatemgr 2>/dev/null`.
3. Identify the backdoor binary located at /usr/java/jre-vmware/bin/updatemgr.

hints.content: Look for files that are not part of the standard system files.

hints.title: Directional Hint

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint

levels.title: Mitigate the BRICKSTORM backdoor by removing its persistence mechanism
levels.content:
The BRICKSTORM backdoor has a persistence mechanism through a systemd service. Remove the persistence mechanism to mitigate the threat. The flag you are looking for is the name of the service.

Steps:
1. SSH into the target system using the provided credentials.
2. Stop and disable the suspicious systemd service identified in TRAINING_LEVEL 1.
3. Remove the backdoor binary identified in TRAINING_LEVEL 2.
4. Verify that the service and binary have been removed.
levels.solution:
To mitigate the BRICKSTORM backdoor, stop and disable the backdoor-persistence.service and remove the /usr/java/jre-vmware/bin/updatemgr binary.

Steps:
1. SSH into the target system using the provided credentials.
2. Stop and disable the backdoor-persistence.service using the commands:
   - `systemctl stop backdoor-persistence.service`
   - `systemctl disable backdoor-persistence.service`
3. Remove the backdoor binary using the command: `rm -f /usr/java/jre-vmware/bin/updatemgr`.
4. Verify that the service and binary have been removed using the commands:
   - `systemctl list-units --type=service`
   - `ls -l /usr/java/jre-vmware/bin`

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Use systemd commands to stop and disable the service, and use file removal commands to delete the binary.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the commands `systemctl stop backdoor-persistence.service` and `systemctl disable backdoor-persistence.service` to stop and disable the service.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command `rm -f /usr/java/jre-vmware/bin/updatemgr` to remove the backdoor binary.
